contract:
Issue #5 Done when: in the opening, the bot picks moves in proportion to how often real 1200-1400 players chose them; once the position is rare (fewer than 20 games) it switches to Stockfish at about 1400 strength; the demo (`pnpm demo:bot`) shows which source chose each move; tests pass in CI using a fake explorer and engine.

FR-2: during the opening, the bot picks its moves from real human games at a configurable rating band, sampled in proportion to how often each move is played. FR-3: once the position is out of the explorer data (too few games below a threshold), the bot switches to Stockfish at a reduced strength. FR-10 spirit: code never returns a move it has not checked legal.

config/tutor.json bot block: { "explorerRatings": [1200, 1400], "explorerSpeeds": ["blitz", "rapid"], "minGames": 20, "outOfBookElo": 1400 }.

Explorer result shape (packages/explorer/src/types.ts): ExplorerResult { moves: ExplorerMove[] (sorted by games desc, top 12 only, so sum(moves.games) can be < totalGames); totalGames; opening; unavailable?: reason (then moves [] and totalGames 0) }. ExplorerMove { uci, san, games, white, draws, black, averageRating }. lookup(fen, { ratings, speeds }) may throw ExplorerConfigError on a 401. Engine.bestMove(fen, { elo?, movetimeMs?, depth? }) -> UCI string.

Implementation brief decisions (verbatim in substance):
1. When available and totalGames >= minGames, sample among listed moves with weight = games (games <= 0 excluded); unlisted moves ignored; random injected (() => number in [0,1), default Math.random).
2. Engine fallback when: unavailable; totalGames < minGames; no listed move with games > 0; sampled explorer move illegal (drop and resample among the remaining legal moves first; engine only if none remain); lookup rejects with a generic error. An error with name === "ExplorerConfigError" is rethrown.
3. Engine: bestMove(fen, { elo: outOfBookElo }), validated with playUci; illegal -> throw an Error naming move and FEN.
4. Game over or invalid FEN: throw before calling anything.
5. Return { uci, san, source: "explorer"|"engine", explorer?: { games, totalGames, share }, fallbackReason?: "unavailable"|"few_games"|"no_moves"|"lookup_failed"|"illegal_explorer_move" }.
6. createSparringBot({ explorer, engine, config, random? }); bad config throws at construction.
7. src stays pure: no I/O, no imports of @chess-tutor/engine or @chess-tutor/explorer in src (structural types). The demo scripts/demo-bot.ts wires the real WASM engine and explorer client, scripted human side (London d2d4 c1f4 e2e3 g1f3 c2c3 f1d3 b1d2 e1g1 / KID g8f6 g7g6 f8g7 d7d6 e8g8 e7e5 b8d7 c7c6, skipping illegal ones, then full-strength engine), --as white|black, --moves N (default 10), labels 'from explorer (G of T games, P%)' / 'from engine (~1400) - <reason>', reads LICHESS_TOKEN from env (never prints it), always quits the engine.

Spoke's reported choices to judge: share = games / totalGames (not games / sum of listed games); demo uses an in-memory SQLite cache and the explorer client's default 1500 ms timeout; the demo game loop was not run (no LICHESS_TOKEN in the spoke environment).

Coordinator gate on 50e47dc: pnpm test 9 files 161 passed; pnpm typecheck exit 0; git diff --name-only matches files_changed (packages/chess-core/{src/bot.ts, src/index.ts, test/bot.test.ts, scripts/demo-bot.ts, tsconfig.json}); src imports only chess.js and local files.
